statement: Ana and Ben play a game with a pile of $n$ stones, taking turns with Ana going first. On each turn a player removes $1$, $3$ or $4$ stones from the pile, but cannot remove more stones than the pile has. The player who takes the last stone wins. For how many values of $n$ from $1$ to $30$ can Ana make sure she wins, no matter how Ben plays?

choices.misconception: I correctly found the losing pile sizes 2, 7, 9, 14, 16, 21, 23, 28 and 30, but I counted those 9 instead of the winning ones.
I thought Ana wins only when she can move straight to a multiple of 7, so I counted only the sizes that are 1, 3 or 4 more than a multiple of 7.
I assumed Ana wins for exactly half of the 30 pile sizes, since going first and going second seemed equally good.
I treated it like the game where you may take 1, 2, 3 or 4 stones, so I thought Ana loses only on multiples of 5, which leaves 30 - 6 = 24.

hints: Work up from small piles. A pile is a loss for the player about to move if every move leads to a pile that is a win for the other player.
A pile of 0 is a loss for the player to move, because the other player just took the last stone. Check 1, 2, 3, ..., 10 one at a time.
The losing sizes are 0, 2, 7, 9, 14, 16, and so on, repeating every 7. Count the losing sizes from 1 to 30 and subtract from 30.

solutions.reliable: Call a pile size losing (L) if the player about to move loses against best play, and winning (W) otherwise. Size $0$ is L. A size is W exactly when some move of $1$, $3$ or $4$ leads to an L size. Then $1$ is W (move to $0$); $2$ is L (the only move is to $1$); $3$ and $4$ are W (move to $0$); $5$ and $6$ are W (move to $2$); $7$ is L (moves lead to $6$, $4$, $3$, all W); $8$ is W (move to $7$); $9$ is L (moves lead to $8$, $6$, $5$, all W); $10$ is W (move to $9$). Sizes $7$ to $10$ repeat the pattern L, W, L, W of sizes $0$ to $3$, and each status depends only on the four sizes just below it, so the pattern repeats every $7$: the L sizes are those that leave remainder $0$ or $2$ when divided by $7$. From $1$ to $30$ these are $2, 7, 9, 14, 16, 21, 23, 28, 30$, which is $9$ sizes. So Ana can make sure she wins for $30 - 9 = 21$ values of $n$.
